[Krichene and Rendle, On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation (KDD 2020)](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; small samples increasingly resemble AUC. Uniform, popularity-matched and text-similar candidates therefore define different evaluation tasks. For one fixed checkpoint, differences establish sensitivity to candidate composition, not improved learning or causal evidence of semantic reasoning. [Dallmann et al. (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045) examine uniform versus popularity sampling specifically for sequential recommenders; [Candidate Set Sampling for Evaluating Top-N Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11723) studies interactions with popularity bias.

Recommended controls, synthesized from this work: freeze checkpoint, histories, users, positives, candidate count, exclusions and tie handling; change only the candidate sampler. Report paired user-level differences and uncertainty from repeated candidate draws. Define popularity matching explicitly using training-only frequencies; popularity-proportional sampling is different from matching the popularity distribution of text-similar candidates. Compare regimes within common popularity strata and a shared text-eligible item/user population; report coverage and excluded cases, with missing-text results separately. These controls narrow the interpretation to candidate composition within observed support. [Schnabel et al., Recommendations as Treatments (2016)](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v48/schnabel16.html) provides the selection-bias and propensity-weighting framework; weighting requires support and appropriate probabilities, and cannot automatically correct nonlinear sampled HR@10.

Unobserved items have unverified relevance. Text-similar candidates may include plausible alternatives, so lower held-out-target HR can reflect competing relevant items rather than worse recommendations. [On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies in Offline Recommender Evaluation (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) connects sampling reliability with exposure and false negatives. Without relevance judgments or exposure logs, describe text-similar sets as stress tests, disclose unknown relevance, and retain the pinned benchmark as the selection criterion.
